entities.summary: Damià Forment was an Aragonese Spanish architect and sculptor, considered the most important Spanish sculptor of the 16th century. Born in unknown, he rose to prominence in the 1530s, during the reign of King Charles V, who sponsored his work. Forment's most famous piece, the 'Assumption of the Virgin' (1539), is now housed in the Cathedral of Zaragoza, Aragon, Spain. His work had a lasting impact on Spanish Baroque architecture and sculpture, influencing later artists such as Francisco de Zurbarán and Velázquez. Forment's legacy extends beyond his art, as his innovations in sculpture and architecture helped shape the cultural identity of Aragon during the Habsburg period. Through his work, Forment embodied the Renaissance ideals of beauty, proportion, and harmony, reflecting the cultural and artistic aspirations of the time. His mastery of gold leaf and intricate detail earned him the admiration of his contemporaries, including the Spanish monarchs, who commissioned his works for their palaces and churches.

entities.summary: Damià Forment was a renowned Aragonese Spanish architect and sculptor, considered the most important Spanish sculptor of the 16th century. Born in Valencia in 1480, Forment's work spanned the late Gothic and early Renaissance periods, characterized by intricate details and classical influences. His most celebrated piece, the bronze Virgin of Lledó, showcased his mastery of figurative sculpture and cemented his reputation as a leading artist of his time. Forment's contributions to Spanish art and architecture not only reflected the cultural and artistic currents of his era but also left a lasting legacy in the development of Spanish Baroque style. The intricate craftsmanship and emotive power of his works continue to inspire artists and art historians to this day.
